_meta.description: Single source of truth for all game ScriptableObjects. Run MobileIdleBuilder > Import Game Data in the Unity Editor to generate or update all assets.

conventions.cross_refs: Use the string 'id' of the target object. Importer resolves to SO reference.
conventions.asset_paths: Project-relative Unity paths (Assets/...). Use 'TODO' for unknown paths — importer will log a warning and leave the field null.
conventions.arrays: Empty arrays [] mean no entries. null and [] are equivalent for the importer.
conventions.comments: Keys prefixed with '_' are ignored by the importer and are purely for documentation.

tiers.description: Fundamental particles harvested from quantum fields. Quarks and leptons, the building blocks of everything.
Assembling nucleons and electrons into complete atoms. The domain of chemistry and the periodic table.

research._comment: First research — unlocked from the start of the tutorial
research.description: Harness the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into protons and neutrons — and combine them with electrons to form the first atoms.
research.codex_entry: The foundational discovery enabling nucleon synthesis. By controlling the strong force, quarks can be permanently bound into stable protons and neutrons.

research.description: Combine a proton and an electron to form the simplest atom: hydrogen.
research.codex_entry: The simplest atom: one proton orbited by one electron. Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and the gateway to all atomic chemistry.

research.description: Unlock the Atomic Assembler and the ability to build complete atoms from nucleons and electrons.
research.codex_entry: Combining protons, neutrons, and electrons into stable atoms. Each element's identity is defined by its proton count — change it and you change the element.

research.description: Unlock the Nucleon Harvester special upgrade for paired field harvesters on opposing polarity fields.
research.codex_entry: Two harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a single Nucleon Harvester, producing protons or neutrons directly without quark combination.

research.description: Unlock the Isotopic Manipulator to add or remove neutrons from base elements, creating isotopes.
research.codex_entry: An element's identity is its proton count, but its neutron count determines its isotope. Isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties but vastly different nuclear behaviour.

research.description: Unlock synthesis of uranium and other heavy elements in the Atomic Assembler.
research.codex_entry: Beyond iron, fusion in stars becomes energy-negative. Only cosmic violence — supernovae, neutron star collisions — forges the heavy elements. We replicate that violence, precisely.

research.description: Unlock uranium enrichment to U-235 and decay particle containment buildings.
research.codex_entry: Some isotopes are inherently unstable, shedding mass as alpha or beta particles. With proper containment, decay is not a hazard — it is a resource.

items.codex_entry: One of two quark flavours that compose protons and neutrons. Carries a +2/3 electric charge. Quarks are permanently confined — they cannot exist freely outside a hadron.
The heavier of the two light quarks, carrying a -1/3 electric charge. Two down quarks and one up quark bind together to form a neutron.
A fundamental lepton with a -1 charge. Orbits the nucleus of atoms and determines all chemical bonding behaviour. No internal structure has ever been detected.
A baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark, bound by the strong nuclear force. The number of protons in a nucleus defines which element it is — this number is the atomic number.
A baryon composed of one up quark and two down quarks. Electrically neutral. Adding or removing neutrons from a nucleus produces isotopes of the same element.
The simplest and most abundant element in the universe. One proton, one electron — the starting point for all atomic chemistry. The primary fuel of stars.
The second lightest element, produced in stellar cores through hydrogen fusion. A noble gas — chemically inert. Its nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons) is identical to an alpha particle.
A soft alkali metal and the lightest solid element. Critical in battery technology — the backbone of rechargeable batteries used in every mobile device.
The basis of all organic chemistry. Carbon's ability to form four bonds makes it the backbone of life. Also exists as graphite, diamond, and graphene.
The third most abundant element in the universe. Highly reactive and essential for combustion and respiration. Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere.
A semiconductor at the heart of modern electronics. Silicon wafers are the foundation of processors, solar cells, and transistors.
The most common element on Earth by mass. The endpoint of stellar fusion — stars cannot fuse elements heavier than iron without consuming more energy than they produce.
The heaviest naturally occurring element. Radioactive — decays slowly over billions of years. The primary fuel for nuclear fission reactors. Requires advanced assembly techniques.
A stable isotope of hydrogen with one added neutron. Found naturally in heavy water. An essential fuel for nuclear fusion reactions alongside tritium.
A radioactive isotope of hydrogen with two neutrons. Undergoes beta decay with a 12.3-year half-life. Combined with deuterium in the most efficient known fusion reaction.
A radioactive isotope of carbon used in archaeological dating. Its predictable decay rate allows scientists to estimate the age of organic materials up to 50,000 years old.
The fissile isotope of uranium used in nuclear reactors and weapons. Splitting U-235 releases enormous energy and produces alpha particles as decay byproducts.

Emitted during alpha decay of heavy radioactive isotopes. Equivalent to a helium-4 nucleus: 2 protons + 2 neutrons. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and used as a secondary energy currency.
Emitted during beta decay of unstable isotopes like Tritium and Carbon-14. A high-energy electron. Collected by Radioactive Containment buildings and fed back into the power grid.

recipes._comment: --- RAW RESOURCE COLLECTION (one recipe per harvested item) ---

recipes._note_neutrons: Hydrogen-1 has no neutrons. Neutron input slot is present in the Atomic Assembler UI but quantity is 0 — omitted here.

recipes._note_neutron_adjustment: Points to the neutron ItemSO — tells the Isotopic Manipulator this recipe adds neutrons.

recipes._comment: Uranium-235 is made by REMOVING 3 neutrons from U-238. The neutron_adjustment field here is empty because no neutrons are added — the building handles removal differently.
recipes._note_byproducts: Alpha particle emitted as U-238 loses 3 neutrons during enrichment.

buildings.description: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Output depends on the field type it is placed on.
buildings._note_special_upgrade: Two adjacent harvesters on opposing polarity fields can be merged into a Nucleon Harvester.
buildings.tutorial_note: First building the player can place. Goes on the quark or lepton field.
buildings.codex_entry: Extracts fundamental particles from quantum fields. Place on a field to begin harvesting. Positive fields yield Up Quarks, negative fields yield Down Quarks, lepton fields yield Electrons.

buildings.description: Binds quarks into protons and neutrons using the strong nuclear force. Requires a power source within link range.
buildings.obsolete_condition: Nucleon Harvester unlocked — the Strong Force Combiner is no longer needed.
buildings.tutorial_note: First powered building. Placement triggers the power system tutorial segment.
buildings.codex_entry: Uses the strong nuclear force to bind quarks into nucleons. Requires a power source within range to operate. Becomes obsolete once the Nucleon Harvester upgrade is unlocked.

buildings.description: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.
buildings.tutorial_note: Introduced immediately after the Strong Force Combiner. Teaches power radius and the energy grid.
buildings.codex_entry: Generates electron volts (eV) to power nearby buildings. Place within link range of powered buildings. Link multiple generators to share power across the grid.

buildings._comment: --- SPECIAL BUILDINGS (available from start, no research required) ---
buildings.description: Sorts raw particles from your inventory and converts their energy into base currency. The act of sorting increases local entropy — a price the Demon gladly pays.
buildings._note_entropy: EntropySinkTag is added by BuildingPlacer/BuildingAuthoring when is_entropy_sink=true. EntropySinkSystem handles conveyor-fed deposits (BuildingInputSlot). MaxwellsDemonController handles manual drag-and-drop deposits (InventorySlot). Both paths coexist.
buildings.tutorial_note: Pre-placed on the starting grid. Player deposits manually-collected particles here to earn the 100 base currency needed for Recombination I.
buildings.codex_entry: A thermodynamic thought experiment made real. Maxwell's Demon appears to violate the second law by sorting particles — but information erasure always costs energy. That cost manifests as entropy. The currency it generates is real. So is the entropy.

buildings.description: Combines protons, neutrons, and electrons into complete atoms. Power cost scales with the element's atomic mass.
buildings.codex_entry: Combines protons, neutrons, and electrons into complete atoms. Power cost scales with the complexity of the element being assembled — heavier elements demand more energy.

buildings.description: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Slower than the Atomic Assembler by design.
buildings.codex_entry: Adds or removes neutrons from a base element to produce isotopes. Radioactive isotopes produced here will emit decay particles over time if housed in a Radioactive Containment building.

buildings.description: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles.
buildings._note_footprint: Houses the Isotopic Manipulator inside it — larger footprint.
buildings.codex_entry: Required housing for any building producing radioactive isotopes. Safely contains decay events and harvests alpha and beta particles as usable energy currency.

fields.codex_entry: A region of space dense with confined quarks. Positive-polarity zones yield Up Quarks; negative-polarity zones yield Down Quarks. Harvesters placed here extract the field's particles automatically.
A region saturated with free leptons. Harvesters placed here collect Electrons continuously. Electrons are essential for completing any atom.

lines.text: Welcome. I am The Architect — your guide through the Quantum Foundry. This facility builds matter from scratch, starting with the smallest particles in existence.
Everything solid in the universe — planets, stars, you — began as fundamental particles. Your job is to harvest them, combine them, and build upward.
See that glowing blue field? That is a Lepton Field — saturated with free electrons. Every atom you will ever build needs them.
Tap it. Pull electrons into your inventory.
Good work. Those electrons gave you your first entropy — the currency that powers this facility. But entropy alone cannot build matter.
That orange field is a Quark Field. It generates Up Quarks and Down Quarks in equal measure every time you mine it — the raw ingredients for every proton and neutron you will ever craft.
Excellent work. You've synthesized protons and neutrons and converted them to entropy — the fundamental energy of this facility.
The field glows where particles accumulate. Tap it to pull electrons into your inventory.
Maxwell's Demon extracts entropy from the energy difference between sorted particles. Deposit what you have collected.
Drag the electrons to the deposit side. The Demon converts particle energy into entropy — the base currency of this facility.
Good. Those electrons built your first entropy. It is a small number for now.
Quarks carry more energy potential than leptons. The Demon will extract more entropy from them. Bring them in.
Deposit all of them. Notice how much more entropy quarks generate compared to electrons. Organized matter will generate more still.
You have enough to begin. Open the menu on the left — the Research panel is there.
The research tree is your progression map. Each node unlocks new processes, new materials, new machinery. Nothing in this facility advances without it.
Recombination I. This unlocks the strong nuclear force — the force that binds quarks into nucleons. Purchase it.
Recombination I is active. The strong nuclear force is now at your disposal — the most powerful fundamental force in nature, and the one that makes atomic structure possible.

A proton is two Up Quarks and one Down Quark — net charge +1, the core of every hydrogen atom. A neutron is one Up Quark and two Down Quarks — net charge zero, the stabilizing mass inside every nucleus beyond hydrogen.
The recipe panel holds every synthesis process you have unlocked. Open it and find the proton recipe.
Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark, bound by the strong force. The result: a proton. Charge +1. The nucleus of the simplest atom in existence. Craft two.
Now the neutron — one Up Quark, two Down Quarks. Net charge zero, but nearly identical mass to the proton. Inside a nucleus, neutrons neutralize the repulsion between protons. Craft two.
Protons and neutrons carry significantly more energy than raw quarks. The Demon values organized matter — each layer of complexity compounds your entropy yield. Bring them in.
Deposit both the protons and the neutrons. You have built the first organized matter this facility has produced.
Complexity yields more entropy. That principle will drive every decision as this facility scales.
Hydrogen synthesis is unlocked. To build a hydrogen atom you need a proton — which you now know how to build — and one electron from the Lepton Field.
Gather your materials: 4 Up Quarks and 2 Down Quarks to build two protons, plus 2 electrons to complete the atoms.
Build the protons first. Two Up Quarks, one Down Quark each. Two protons means two hydrogen atoms.
The final step: combine a proton and an electron. The electromagnetic attraction between the positive nucleus and the negative lepton creates a stable atomic orbital. Craft your hydrogen.
Hydrogen. Atomic number 1. The most abundant element in the observable universe — and you built two of them from quarks and energy alone.
Hydrogen atoms carry more bound energy than raw particles. Organized matter always yields more entropy — the Demon knows the difference. Bring it in.
That entropy unlocks Automation I. A Field Collector — a Harvester placed directly on a quantum field — gathers particles automatically on a continuous cycle. No tapping required.
This is the transition point. Manual harvesting was a lesson. The Field Collector is how you scale.
Open the Build menu and place a Harvester on the quark or lepton field. Once it is running, the facility collects without you.
Open the build menu and place a building on an open grid tile. It will begin production immediately.
Your factory is running. Buildings produce at their rated output continuously — no manual input required.

As production scales, entropy accumulates. But there is a ceiling on each run. When your net worth approaches the prestige threshold, you will have extracted most of this run's value — and it will be time to reset.
You have reached the ceiling. Prestige is not failure — it is the mechanism that converts one-time progress into permanent power.

The reset clears your inventory, buildings, and entropy. What you keep: prestige currency and a research memory discount on nodes you have already unlocked. Initiate it — you will return faster than you left.
The reset is complete. The facility rebuilds, but you are not starting over — you are starting ahead.
You carry prestige currency now. Unlike entropy, it does not reset between runs. Spend it on permanent upgrades that will accelerate every future run.
Open the upgrade shop. Each purchase compounds across every future run. Spend wisely.

Tap Maxwell's Demon to sell your electrons.

Tap the quark field to collect 5 Up Quarks and 5 Down Quarks.

locked_messages.message: Focus on the quark field for now.

tutorial_steps.hint: Bring your quarks to Maxwell's Demon to convert them to entropy.

locked_messages.message: Deposit your quarks in Maxwell's Demon!

tutorial_steps.hint: Drag your quarks to the right side to sell them.
Great! Close the panel when you're ready.
Open the menu on the left to find the Research panel.
Purchase Recombination I to unlock nucleon synthesis.
Collect 8 Up Quarks and 8 Down Quarks — you'll need them to synthesize 2 Protons and 2 Neutrons.
Open the Build menu to craft nucleons from quarks.
Craft 2 Protons. Each requires 2 Up Quarks + 1 Down Quark.
Now craft 2 Neutrons. Each requires 1 Up Quark + 2 Down Quarks.
Tap Maxwell's Demon to sell your Protons and Neutrons for entropy.
Deposit your Protons and Neutrons into the Demon.

Collect 4 Up Quarks, 2 Down Quarks, and 2 Electrons to craft Hydrogen atoms.

Bring your Hydrogen atoms to Maxwell's Demon.
